extracted.intended_audience: businesses, inventors, and designers seeking practical guidance on patent and industrial design filings
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction checklist of the basic steps to prepare, file, and prosecute patent and industrial/design applications in the US, Canada, China, India, and via international systems (PCT & Hague).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be: Novel, Useful, Non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the invention meets the basic patentability standards (novelty, utility/usefulness, and non-obviousness) before pursuing filing in any jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a Patent / Prior Art Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors often search existing patents and publications to confirm that the invention is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough prior art search helps identify foreseeable rejections and refines claim drafting; applicable in every jurisdiction listed (US, Canada, China, India, PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare the Patent Application (required components)
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical application includes: Specification (description of the invention); Claims defining the legal scope; Abstract; Patent drawings; Oath or declaration; Application Data Sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification, claims, abstract and drawings meet the formal and substantive content requirements of the target patent office. These components form the core of the filing in the US, Canada, China, and India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Patent Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent drawings are a standard part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare clear, compliant drawings as part of the application package; drawings assist in disclosure and are often required for both utility and design filings (see also design drawing guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: File the Application with the Appropriate Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is submitted electronically through the filing system of the relevant patent office (e.g., USPTO, CIPO, CNIPA, Indian Patent Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the office-specific electronic filing system and follow local filing formalities and document formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent examiner reviews the application and may issue Office Actions requesting amendments or clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to substantive and formal objections; prosecution timelines and practice differ by jurisdiction but the examiner/office-action cycle is common to all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance, Grant, and Issue Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, the patent is granted after payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After prosecution concludes favorably, pay applicable issue/grant fees and follow any post-grant formalities required by the granting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term and Maintenance Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Term: 20 years from the filing date (with maintenance fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most jurisdictions (as noted for US, Canada, China, India) provide a 20-year term from the filing date; some offices require periodic maintenance or renewal fees to keep the patent in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Patent Protects Ornamental Appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent protects the ornamental appearance of an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/industrial design rights cover visual features—shape, configuration, pattern or ornament—rather than functional aspects; choose design protection when appearance is the primary asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Design Novelty and Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if the design is new and original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prior designs and public disclosures to confirm novelty and originality of the ornamentation before filing a design/industrial design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Design Drawings or Photographs with Multiple Views
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare design drawings showing multiple views of the article; or photographs where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design filings should include clear illustrations (multiple views) that disclose the claimed ornamental features; presentation requirements may vary by office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft Short Specification / Title and Single Claim for Design Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft a short description and title of the article; for US design patents, draft a short specification and a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications typically require concise descriptive text; U.S. design patents commonly have a single claim directed to the appearance as shown in the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: File the Design Application and Undergo Formal/Novelty Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: File the application with the relevant design office; the application undergoes formal examination and novelty/compliance review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/industrial design offices perform formalities checks and novelty examinations; respond to objections and satisfy formal requirements for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design / Industrial Design Protection Terms by Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Design Patent Term (US): 15 years from grant. Protection Term (Canada): Up to 15 years. Design Term (China): 15 years. Design Protection (India): 10 years (extendable by 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term lengths and renewal/extension rules differ across jurisdictions—verify local term and renewal mechanics when planning protection strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Applications (≈18 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication after 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent (and many international) applications are commonly published about 18 months from earliest filing/priority date; be aware of publication consequences for confidentiality and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request Examination Within Jurisdictional Timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Request examination within the time limits required by the office (e.g., Canada: request examination within 4 years of filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices require a formal request for examination (and/or payment) within a statutory deadline; failure to request examination can lead to abandonment or delayed prosecution. China requires requesting substantive examination; India requires requesting examination and responding to objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT International Application Process
rubrics_metrics.description: File an international patent application under the PCT; an international search is conducted; publication after 18 months; optional international preliminary examination; enter the national phase in selected countries (typically within 30 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCT centralizes early prosecution steps and defers national filings; use it to postpone national costs and get an international search report and optional preliminary opinion before entering national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague System for International Design Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare design drawings/photographs and file an international design application under the Hague System; designate countries for protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hague System allows one international filing administered by WIPO, with formal examination by WIPO and subsequent examination by designated countries—useful for obtaining design protection in multiple jurisdictions via a single application.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Formal Examination, Publication, and Designation Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO performs a formal examination and publishes in the International Designs Bulletin; designated countries then examine and may grant protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a two-stage process under Hague: WIPO handles formalities/publication while national/territorial offices examine substantive registrability and grant protection accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Phase Entry and Local Examination after PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the national phase in selected countries (typically within 30 months) and undergo national examination in each country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT does not grant patents—applicants must enter national phase and comply with each country's substantive examination, timing, and formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use International Systems to Simplify Global Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: International systems such as the PCT and Hague System simplify global protection by allowing applicants to file one application that can cover multiple countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For companies operating internationally, PCT (patents) and Hague (designs) can reduce filing complexity and centralize early-stage procedural steps; they are valuable tools when seeking multi-jurisdictional protection.
